notes: Objectives are printed in one 'Objectifs' cell per theme; they are kept at theme level (topic null), not split between units. Pages 54-58 (p53 is the section cover 'Mathématiques'). 3 themes, 12 units. Each theme is a 4-column table (Thème | Objectifs | Contenu | Activités envisageables); the 'Activités envisageables' column (including its NB remarks) is excluded. domain = the Thème (week counts dropped), topic = the numbered unit in the Contenu column. In the tables the Objectifs column is one undivided cell per theme page (the dashed row separators run only across Contenu/Activités), so each objective was assigned to the unit it is printed beside on the page image, checked against its wording. Contents are the Contenu lines as printed (sub-headings like 'Les cellules sexuelles :' kept as their own item, bullets/dashes stripped). Theme II has two full-width sub-headings printed across the Objectifs/Contenu/Activités columns ('La fonction reproductrice chez l’homme :' p56, '... chez la femme :' p57); they are kept as a prefix of the topic. Objectives are short action-verb statements (Construire / Expliquer / Identifier / Décrire / Résoudre / Adopter / Être conscient), 1-2 per unit; several units have none of their own. Placement calls: p56 'Expliquer les fonctions du testicule et leur régulation.' is printed beside unit 1 but the undivided cell also spans unit 2 (fonction endocrine et régulation), so it plausibly covers both; kept on unit 1 only. p57 'Expliquer la régulation de la fonction reproductrice chez la femme.' is printed beside unit 3 (it may also cover unit 2, cycle sexuel, which has no objective beside it). p58 'Être conscient de l’importance du diagnostic prénatal.' sits on the unit 1/2 separator; assigned to unit 2 (diagnostic prénatal is treated there). Programme contents for this section do not include the evolution or immunity themes of the Sciences expérimentales programme.
